- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  File: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md (and byte-identical twin workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md)
  Line or code reference: line 12 (new Step 0 bullet "Issue-mode resume without a `— resume.` block"), line 16 (Step 1 "Resolve the plan doc." unchanged), line 187 (Zombie-checker cleanup section header "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene, so stray checkers never pile up:")
  Problem: The new Step 0 bullet instructs the session to run the Zombie-checker cleanup "once step 1 has read the plan", but Step 1 (line 16) is unchanged and contains no operational instruction to invoke the cleanup, and the cleanup-section header at line 187 still reads "Every stage session runs this in step 0, after resume hygiene" — unchanged. The cleanup predicate (`mcp__github__issue_read get_labels` against the `<owner>/<repo>#<N>` parsed from the plan header's `Source issue:` line) requires data that is only available after Step 1's `Read` in full. An unattended session walking the steps in literal order will either (a) attempt the cleanup at end of Step 0 before the `Source issue:` identifier exists, or (b) note the deferral text in the bullet but never return to Step 1 to run it, because Step 1 does not reference the cleanup.
  Why it fails at runtime: Cause 2 of the PR description states "The Zombie-checker cleanup ran only from inside resume hygiene, so it never ran on this path." The fix's intended contract is that the cleanup now actually fires on a `/reclarify` resume, after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available. The implementation provides a textual deferral in Step 0 but no operational hook in Step 1, and the cleanup-section header assigns the work to Step 0 in contradiction of the deferral. The stopped `… — blocked on issue` session therefore stays in the session list until a human archives it — re-introducing exactly the bug the PR is meant to fix. The PR description acknowledges this is the same failure mode that produced the original hand-archive burden.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
  Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py (extend `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` or add a sibling test).
  Evidence of absence: `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` (lines 245-264) only asserts text-string existence: the new title pattern, the Step 0 bullet header, the cleanup sub-bullet header, the label predicate, the self-exclusion clause, the working-bucket skip, the `Source issue:` plan-header references, the rename-failure fallback, the label-read-failure path, and a title-collision check. It does not assert that Step 1 has any reference to invoking the cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-section header at line 187 carries an exception for issue-mode timing, and does not pin the deferred cleanup to an operational hook after Step 1.
